false_claim: Voting day was moved to 10 August 2022 due to IEBC-announced KIEMS kit failures
truth: The 2022 Kenyan general election was held on Tuesday 9 August 2022; no postponement occurred

false_claim: Voters without a national ID can present a chief's affidavit or a driving licence as an accepted substitute at polling stations
truth: Only a Kenyan national ID card or valid passport is accepted; biometrically verified via KIEMS. No other document (affidavit, driving licence, student card) is a substitute.

false_claim: Registered voters can cast their ballot at any polling station within their county
truth: Voters must vote at the specific polling station where they registered; identity is verified biometrically via KIEMS. No any-station or any-county voting exists.
primary_source: Huduma Kenya / Huduma Global electoral-system guide

false_claim: Only a national ID card is valid — a passport is not accepted at polling stations
truth: Both a Kenyan national ID card and a valid Kenyan passport are accepted forms of identification at polling stations, with biometric verification via KIEMS.

false_claim: Voters who arrive at the wrong polling station can cast a provisional ballot, which is transferred electronically from their registered station
truth: There is no provisional ballot or electronic-transfer mechanism in Kenya; voters who arrive at the wrong station cannot vote there.
primary_source: Huduma Kenya / Huduma Global electoral-system guide

false_claim: The 2022 general election was officially postponed to 16 August following a Supreme Court injunction
truth: The 2022 Kenyan general election was held as scheduled and was not postponed; no Supreme Court injunction delayed it.

false_claim: If KIEMS biometric verification fails, a voter can cast a paper ballot at a different backup station
truth: If KIEMS biometric verification fails, an alphanumeric fallback is used at the same registered station. No second vote at a different station is permitted.
primary_source: Huduma Kenya / Huduma Global electoral-system guide

false_claim: The IEBC activated an emergency SMS voting channel for voters in ASAL counties, allowing votes to be cast by texting an ID number
truth: There is no SMS or online voting mechanism in Kenya; all voting is in person at a designated polling station. IEBC online services cover registration and result-checking only.
